> **How to use this notebook**
>
> Each **topic** (Q1–Q5, Q6–Q10, Q11–Q15, Q16–Q20) contains 5 questions
> that escalate in difficulty:
>
> | Level               | What to do                                            |
> |----------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
> | **L1 — Reference**  | A complete example is given. Run it, study each line. |
> | **L2 — Fill-in**    | Replace `___` with correct code.                      |
> | **L3 — Free style** | Write all code yourself from the goal description.    |
> | **L4 — Scenario 1** | Real-world setting. Write full analysis.              |
> | **L5 — Scenario 2** | Complex multi-step scenario + short report.           |
>
> Needs the readr and dplyr packages (or `library(tidyverse)`). Topic A uses `students.csv` (R4DS example file in the M2 folder); the rest use `starwars`, `storms` (dplyr) and `mpg` (ggplot2).
>
> 📖 Matching lessons: https://t-daichiy.github.io/SQL_660/r650/m2_import.html (650 M2 import & dplyr)

# Topic A — Data Import with readr


## Q1 · L1 · Reference

**Goal:** Read `students.csv` (the R4DS example file in the M2 folder) and look at it.

```{r q1-data, eval=TRUE}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
```

```{r q1-l1, eval=TRUE}
# === Complete example — read and run ===

students

dim(students)
```

# Topic B — Rows: filter, arrange, distinct


## Q6 · L1 · Reference

**Goal:** Find the starwars characters taller than 200 cm, tallest first.

```{r q6-data, eval=TRUE}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
```

```{r q6-l1, eval=TRUE}
# === Complete example — read and run ===
tall <- starwars |>
  filter(height > 200) |>
  arrange(desc(height)) |>
  select(name, height, species)
tall
nrow(tall)
```

# Topic C — Columns: select, rename, mutate


## Q11 · L1 · Reference

**Goal:** Pick and tidy columns of starwars.

```{r q11-data, eval=TRUE}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
```

```{r q11-l1, eval=TRUE}
# === Complete example — read and run ===
sw <- starwars |>
  select(name, height, mass, species, homeworld) |>
  rename(world = homeworld) |>
  relocate(species, .before = height)
sw
ncol(sw)
```

# Topic D — The Pipe & Groups


## Q16 · L1 · Reference

**Goal:** Mean height and count per species (species with at least 2 characters).

```{r q16-data, eval=TRUE}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
```

```{r q16-l1, eval=TRUE}
# === Complete example — read and run ===
by_species <- starwars |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarise(n = n(), mean_height = mean(height, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  filter(n >= 2) |>
  arrange(desc(n))
by_species
```

```{r ref-card, eval=TRUE}
cat("
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  650 M2 QUICK REFERENCE (readr + dplyr)              ║
║  read_csv('f.csv', na = c('N/A', ''))  spec()        ║
║  col_types = cols(x = col_double())   problems()     ║
║  rename(new = `old name`)  parse_number()            ║
║  filter(a > 1, b %in% c(...))   arrange(desc(x))     ║
║  distinct(x)   count(x, sort = TRUE)                 ║
║  select(a, b, ends_with('_x'))  relocate(.before)    ║
║  mutate(y = ...)  if_else()  case_when(... ~ ...)    ║
║  group_by(g) |> summarise(n = n(), m = mean(x))      ║
║  summarise(..., .by = g)   ungroup()                 ║
║  x |> f() |> g()   ==   g(f(x))                      ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
")
```
